chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the excess weight in the scales of meat and qatt (a unit of weight) and similar things, so I informed him that they buy the weighing weights here for ten dirhams, and the meat (sold by) artals for dirhams, and it is not weighed except with an excess (given), and that excess has no known fixed time. He said: 'If that is the trade practice of the people of the town, then look to the middle of that excess and do not count it (as part of the price/weight).'
ai.seo_question: How to handle variable excess weight in meat sales according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical application of avoiding *gharar* (uncertainty) in local meat markets where 'excess weight' (*rajhan*) was customary but unquantified. He instructs the buyer to estimate the average portion of this customary excess and exclude it from the principal cost, thereby aligning commercial practice with the principle of fairness (*adl*) while respecting local *urf* (custom). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic flexibility in adapting fixed legal principles to variable market conditions to prevent exploitation.
